# **Lead. Collaborate. Transform.**  

**Join us for Nashville Hub’s highly rated Distributive Leadership training, focused on building stronger teams within your Academies model.**  

This two-day, open-enrollment event in Nashville is beneficial for both teams and individuals. Participants will learn how to strengthen collaboration, clarify roles, and build capacity across their teams. Through interactive sessions with Nashville Hub consultants **Jeremiah Davis** and **Thommye Kelley**, attendees will gain practical strategies to lead collectively and drive student success. Participants will also hear from local Nashville leaders in similar roles.  

### **Topics covered include:**  
- Leadership Structures  
- Capacity Building  
- Teaming  
- Communication  
- Influence vs. Power  
- Common Challenges  

---

### **Meet the Trainers**  

**Jeremiah Davis** began his educational career as a CTE (Career and Technical Education) Criminal Justice teacher. He became the Academy Team Lead as well as the CTE Lead for his school. As Team Lead, his academy was awarded Model Status during the first NCAC review. Jeremiah has also conducted TN DoE training with new Criminal Justice teachers across Tennessee to help them start strong and support student success. He later served as Dean of Students and Academy Principal, guiding his academies to earn Model Status at each reaccreditation. He is now an Executive Principal and CTE Coordinator, serving diverse stakeholders statewide.  

**Thommye Kelley** is a third-generation educator passionate about helping students discover success. She currently serves as the Academy Coach at Glencliff High School within Metro Nashville Public Schools. Before that, she taught social studies at Whites Creek High School, including U.S. History, African American History, Personal Finance, and Economics. After her first year of teaching, she became the Academy Team Lead for the Academy of Alternative Energy, Sustainability, and Logistics. In 2018, she accepted her current role as Academy Coach at Glencliff High.
